recommendation: Temperature-dependent pure-water enthalpy and heat capacity, explicitly bounded by phase and pressure
reasoning: Water is used by most thermal, dilution, titration, and extraction workflows. A shared reviewed enthalpy model can improve these without pretending to supply missing chemistry or mixture activity data. This recommendation is architectural inference, not a claim that current implementation lacks every listed property.

primary_sources.title: IAPWS SR6-08(2011), Properties of Liquid Water at 0.1 MPa
primary_sources.reviewed_scope: Simple thermodynamic and transport correlations near 0.1 MPa; liquid-water validity 253.15–383.15 K includes metastable states. Metastable validity alone does not authorize bulk liquid across an equilibrium phase transition.

primary_sources.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook water, SI thermochemistry
primary_sources.reviewed_scope: Liquid Shomate heat capacity/enthalpy fit valid 298–500 K; gas fits begin at 500 K. Cp units J/mol/K; enthalpy kJ/mol; t=T/1000. Do not apply the gas fit near 373 K or liquid fit below 298 K without a documented alternative.

primary_sources.title: IAPWS R6-95(2018), IAPWS-95 water and steam
primary_sources.reviewed_scope: Broad fluid thermodynamics and vapor-liquid equilibrium. Suitable reference for validation; implementing full formulation is a larger project than an ambient-water bounded correlation.

implementation_sequence: Audit the current energy reference and phase-ledger semantics before selecting coefficients. Freeze numerical checkpoints independently from the runtime implementation.
Add a typed, provenance-bearing pure-water property provider with explicit temperature/pressure/phase validity and SI conversion. Preserve unsupported-state qualifications.
Use an integrated enthalpy difference for finite heating/cooling; do not replace it with Cp at one endpoint times delta-T. Inverse temperature solving needs a monotone bounded bracket.
Separate glass heat capacity from contents, and account for phase latent heat exactly once. Preserve recorded evaporated/vented mass and its energy.

Validate unit agreement, split-dose equivalence, inverse heat/cool, mixing orientation, phase transitions and finite-state refusal. Include pressure-dependent saturation as a separate extension, not an implicit liquid-property change.
performance_experiments: Serial warm-process microprofiles: pure water heat/cool loops versus brine thermal loops, mixture equilibration, acid/base settlement, gas pressure and CLI startup.
Report whole CLI wall time separately from kernel time; debug and release results cannot be combined.
Collect repeated medians and peak RSS on a controlled hosted runner, record binary/source identity, and gate optimizations on unchanged energy/material certificates.
exclusions: No arbitrary mixture enthalpy inferred from pure-water coefficients.
No density correction for concentrated electrolytes without reviewed partial molar volume data.
No claim that all retained nine scientific qualifications disappear.
